meta.description: Phase 1: Structured Izon (Kolokuma) grammar reference, built from academic sources cited within each section. This is a reference/rules dataset, not a sentence corpus.
sources_summary: Williamson, K. (1965) A Grammar of the Kolokuma Dialect of Ijo
Okunrinmeta, U. (2013) Singular-Plural Distinction in Izon
Okotori, E.B. (2022) Focus Construction in Kolokuma
Okotori, E.B. (2022) English Loanword in Kolokuma
Isoun, S.T. & Egbuson, E. (2025) Sentence Patterns in Izon
Isoun, S.T. & Egbuson, E. (2022) Cohesion in Izon Texts
Evulewuru, A.P.M. & Uwasomba, B.U. (2025) Distinctive Study of Izon and Ogbia
meta.honesty_note: Sections vary in reliability. Tense/aspect and syntax rules are high-confidence (cross-validated against many example sentences). Tone marking is low-confidence throughout due to OCR corruption. See known_gaps in pronouns.json.

pronouns.description: Izon (Kolokuma) pronoun forms, consolidated from multiple sources. Sources noted per entry since forms vary by dialect/source and tone marks are often unreliable from OCR.

2sg.note: same form as 1sg per source; tone distinguishes in speech

reflexive_pronouns.note: formed by adding 'ozu' (self) to the possessive form, per Okunrinmeta 2013 (Izon/Ogbia paper)

known_gaps: The 1965 grammar book's Appendix II pronoun table has full tone-marked short/long/object/subject forms but OCR extraction corrupted the tone diacritics badly (numbers substituted for tone marks). Not included here to avoid shipping wrong data.
Tone marks are omitted throughout this file since reliable source data for them was not extractable.
2sg and 1sg sharing 'ine'/'inei' for possessive is suspicious and may be an OCR/transcription error in the source paper rather than a real fact about the language - flagged for native speaker review.

tense_aspect.description: Izon (Kolokuma) tense-aspect system, per Williamson 1965 grammar. The system has 4 aspects that combine with 3 tenses, plus 1 tense-independent aspect.

system_overview.note: Aspects S, I, C, St each combine with Pa/Pr/F. Habitual does not vary by tense.

SPa.name: Simple Past
SPa.meaning: a completed action in the past (simple past tense, like English 'walked', 'saw')

IPa.name: Immediate Past
IPa.meaning: an action completed in the recent past, often translated with English present perfect ('has done')

SPr.name: Simple Present
SPr.meaning: a present tense state or ongoing action

StPr.name: Stative Present
StPr.meaning: a present state resulting from a completed action

CPa.name: Continuous Past
CPa.meaning: an ongoing action in the past ('was doing')

examples.izon_gloss: fowl T burn CPa charcoal peck SPa
examples.english: the fowl pecked at some burning charcoal

examples.izon_gloss: he come CPa as we go road on him reach SPa
examples.english: as he was coming, we went and met him on the road

examples.izon_gloss: he go canoe paddle SF way say man show IPa
examples.english: he has gone and told the man to paddle the canoe

examples.izon_gloss: thing cook SF because she pepper buy SPa
examples.english: intending to cook, she bought pepper

Hab.name: Habitual
Hab.meaning: a habitual or generally-true action, tense-independent

examples.izon_gloss: night em at lamp Tpl light Hab

Tpl.name: Plural marker
Tpl.meaning: marks plurality on a noun (not a tense/aspect marker but frequently co-occurs)

examples.izon_gloss: woman pi Tpl and children Tpl and are-there
examples.english: the women and children are there

T.name: Definite/topic marker
T.meaning: marks a noun as definite or topical (roughly like English 'the')

tense_aspect.source: Williamson, K. (1965) A Grammar of the Kolokuma Dialect of Ijo. Sentence examples extracted from body text with intact gloss tags.
tense_aspect.confidence_note: These markers and their meanings are directly stated in the grammar's prose (section 2.1.12) and cross-validated against ~100 example sentences that retained clean gloss tags during extraction. This is reliable structured data, unlike the tone-marked pronoun tables which had OCR corruption.

noun_morphology.description: Izon noun and pronoun plural formation rules, from Okunrinmeta 2013 (Arogbo-Izon dialect data) and Williamson 1965 grammar (Kolokuma dialect). Dialect noted per rule since these differ slightly.

noun_plural_marker_a.name: a- plurality prefix
noun_plural_marker_a.rule: The prefix 'a-' attaches to a consonant-initial singular noun when preceded by a numeral qualifier (two through twenty-nine).
exceptions: For vowel-initial nouns already starting with 'a', the plurality marker is elided rather than doubled: e.g. 'ma aga' (two behaviours), not 'ma aaga'.
From thirty (suwei) through thirty-nine, the 'a' marker is dropped entirely and the numeral follows the noun instead: e.g. 'kimi suwei' (thirty men).
From forty (mesi) upward, 'a' prefixes to the numeral itself, not the noun: e.g. 'kurai amesi' (forty years).

noun_plural_marker_definite.name: definite article pluralization
noun_plural_marker_definite.rule: 'ma' following a singular noun indicates definiteness/femininity in some contexts; 'ma' after a plural noun indicates plurality.

examples.izon: zei oni ma / zei abu ma

reflexive_formation.rule: Reflexive pronouns are formed by adding 'ozu' (self) to the POSSESSIVE form of the pronoun (not the object form, unlike English).
reflexive_formation.note: This causes a common transfer error for Izon speakers learning English: 'their selfs' instead of 'themselves', since Izon builds reflexives from possessives (their) not object pronouns (them).

sentence_word_order.rule: Izon is SOV (Subject-Object-Verb), unlike English's SVO.
sentence_word_order.compound_patterns: Izon uses SOOV, SOVOV, SOCV, SCOV, SOAV, SAOV for sentences with 2+ objects/complements/adverbials, where English uses SVOO, SVOC, SVOA - see sentence_patterns dataset for full examples.

phonology.description: Izon (Kolokuma) phonology reference: vowels, consonants, tone, syllable structure. Sources: English Loanword in Kolokuma (Okotori 2022), Izon/Ogbia comparison (Evulewuru & Uwasomba 2025).

vowels.vowel_harmony_rule: Wide and narrow vowels do not co-occur within a single word. The open vowel /a/ is neutral and can occur with either set.
vowels.nasalization_rule: When two vowels occur in a word before a final /n/, both are nasalized. Examples: bien (to defecate), afian (shit), fain (to be bent), kaịn (torn), gbain (to keep safe).

consonants.trigraph: ngh (interchangeable with 'ng' in some standardization schemes)
consonants.note: gb and kp are labio-velar consonants absent from English; they are single sounds, not consonant clusters.

tone.system: Izon has two tones: high and low.
tone.marking_convention: High tone is marked with an acute accent (á). Low tone is left unmarked.

examples.gloss: name of a village in Kolokuma

tone.caveat: Tone marking was frequently lost or corrupted during OCR extraction across our dictionary and grammar sources. Treat tone marks in other extracted files as unreliable unless cross-checked.

syllable_structure.rule: Onset and coda are optional; nucleus is obligatory. Izon strongly prefers open syllables (ending in a vowel) and does NOT allow consonant clusters or closed syllables (ending in a consonant) in native structure.

loanword_adaptation_rules.description: How English loanwords are phonologically nativized into Izon (via epenthesis - inserting vowels to break up clusters/codas the language doesn't allow).
loanword_adaptation_rules.rule_1_coda_epenthesis: A final consonant (coda) gets a vowel added after it, since Izon doesn't allow closed syllables.
loanword_adaptation_rules.rule_2_cluster_simplification: Consonant clusters get vowels inserted between them to break them into separate syllables.

examples.process: affricate ch approximated to s (Izon lacks /tʃ/)

syntax_rules.description: Izon (Kolokuma) syntactic rules: focus marking and sentence patterns. Source: Okotori 2022 (Focus Construction), Isoun & Egbuson 2025 (Sentence Patterns).

focus_marking.description: Izon marks emphasis/focus using particles placed AFTER the focused constituent (in-situ, not moved to front like English clefts 'It was X that...').

ki.used_for: subject NP, object NP, verb, genitive NP, subject-position pronouns

example.plain: Tari fun-bi gou-mi (Tari read the book)
example.focused: Tari ki fun-bi gou-mi (It was Tari that read the book)

ko.used_for: object of postposition WHEN the postposition is locative (place)

example.plain: Tokoni tebulu ogono boo fiyai-bi gbana-mi (Tokoni placed food on the table)
example.focused: Tokoni tebulu ogono ko fiyai-bi gbana-mi (It was ON THE TABLE that Tokoni put the food)

example.plain: Tari sili ni I piri-mi (Tari gave me money)
example.focused: Sili-bi, Tari I kiri ki piri-mi (It was ME that Tari gave the money)

focus_marking.verb_focus_special_rule: The verb is the only constituent that can be FRONTED (moved) in Izon. When a verb is focused, the object moves to clause-initial position, the focused verb moves to pre-verbal position, and a copy of the verb remains at its original site. Example: 'Obori-bi, Idisemi fe ki fe-mi' (It was BUY that she bought the goat, not steal).

sentence_patterns.description: Izon has 10 basic sentence patterns for what English expresses in 7, because Izon splits some English SVOO/SVOC/SVOA patterns into two variants depending on element order.
sentence_patterns.izon_is_SOV: Base word order is Subject-Object-Verb, vs English Subject-Verb-Object.

patterns.example_english: His father gave him a car

patterns.note: Izon determiner (bi='the') follows the noun; English determiner precedes it.

patterns.example_izon: Ari fun bi tebulu ongono werimi
patterns.example_gloss: I book the table on left
patterns.example_english: I left the book on the table

patterns.note: Izon SC pattern has no overt copula/linking verb, unlike English 'is'.

determiner_position.rule: The determiner/article follows the noun in Izon (noun-final), unlike English where it precedes (determiner-initial).
